    target_words: 200
    bullets:
      - "Flow-matching VLAs degrade under distribution shift on LIBERO benchmarks."
      - "We propose ACR-VLA: (1) K=10 multi-sample generation, (2) conformal-score-based selection, (3) observation-conditioned learned residual correction (CRM, ~250K params, ~3ms overhead) — wraps any frozen VLA without retraining."

    deadline: "2026-05-26 (abstract DDL)"

  introduction:
    target_pages: 1.5
    bullets:
      - "Opening: VLAs achieve near-saturated in-distribution but degrade under distribution shift. Existing solutions: training-time (RobustVLA, SRPO, DiG-Flow) require retraining; inference-time (ReconVLA selects but cannot synthesize; SC-VLA needs RL; VLA-Pilot has 2.4s latency)."
      - "Gap: No method performs learned action correction at inference time on frozen VLAs. Sample selection is upper-bounded by sample quality."
      - "Contributions: (1) sample-then-correct pipeline with +7.0pp over selection alone on object tasks; (2) honest negative — observation features outperform per-DOF conformal features for correction (19.0% vs 11.0%); (3) correction magnitude control is critical and previously unrecognized (norm=1.42 → 0%)."
    key_references:
      - chen2026reconvla
      - sc_vla_2026
      - vla_pilot_2025
      - silver2018residual
      - shukor2025smolvla

  related_work:
    target_pages: 1.5
    subsections:
      vla_robustness:
        scope: "Training-time (RobustVLA, SRPO, DiG-Flow, ACoT-VLA) vs inference-time (ReconVLA, SC-VLA, VLA-Pilot, A2C2). Position ACR-VLA as plug-and-play inference-time correction."
        key_refs: [robustvla2025, srpo2025, digflow2025, chen2026reconvla, sc_vla_2026, vla_pilot_2025, a2c2_2025]
      conformal_prediction_robotics:
        scope: "CP foundations (Angelopoulos, CGS), CP in robotics (conformalized teleop, CP-loop, ACP+CBF). Position ACR-VLA's use of CP for selection stage."
        key_refs: [angelopoulos2023gentle, braun2025cgs, zhao2024conformalized, wang2025cploop, zhou2025acp_cbf]
      residual_policy_learning:
        scope: "Residual RL (Silver 2018, TRANSIC, PLD, DRC). Emphasize magnitude control as underexplored."
        key_refs: [silver2018residual, jiang2024transic, xiao2026pld, pan2025drc]
      uncertainty_quantification_vla:
        scope: "UQ for VLAs (DiU, SAFE, VLA calibration). Distinguish multi-sample from single-pass UQ."
        key_refs: [xing2026diu, gu2025safe, zollo2025vla_calibration]

  method:
    target_pages: 2.0
    subsections:
      problem_setup:
        bullets:
          - "Frozen flow-matching VLA π_θ generates K action samples per step."
          - "Action space: 7-DOF (6 arm + 1 gripper), action chunks of length C."
      multi_sample_generation_and_selection:
        bullets:
          - "K=10 samples via flow-matching; Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage covariance → CGS nonconformity scores."
          - "Argmin selection: pick lowest-CGS-score sample as base action a_base."
      conformal_residual_module:
        bullets:
          - "CRM: lightweight MLP (~250K params), takes observation features z_obs, outputs bounded residual δ."
          - "Final action: a = a_base + clip(δ, ‖δ‖ ≤ ε)."
          - "Training: offline L2 loss to expert actions, augmented with Gaussian noise on mean-action (σ ∈ [0.02, 0.1]) and uncertainty features (σ ≈ 0.006)."
      magnitude_control:
        bullets:
          - "Critical: unbounded CRM (ε=1.42) → 0% (compounding error destroys trajectory)."
          - "Norm sweep: ε ∈ {0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3}. Optimal range ε ∈ [0.05, 0.2]."
          - "Connect to residual RL magnitude bounds (Silver 2018, TRANSIC gating, PLD scheduling)."

  experiments:
    target_pages: 2.5
    subsections:
      setup:
        bullets:
          - "Backbone: SmolVLA (450M params, flow-matching). Benchmark: LIBERO Spatial + Object (10 tasks each, 10 rollouts/task)."
          - "Baselines: VLA-only (K=1), VLA-mean (K=10 average), Argmin (K=10 CGS selection)."
          - "CRM variants: obs_only, perdof, scalar — same architecture, different conditioning input."
          - "Statistical protocol: seed=42 primary + seed=43 doubling (PENDING), Fisher exact test, bootstrap CI."
      main_results:
        bullets:
          - "Object: obs_only 19.0% vs argmin 12.0% (+7.0pp). VLA-only 12.0%. perdof 11.0%. scalar 9.0%."
          - "Spatial: ALL methods 30-35% (null result). CRM correction does not help on spatial perturbations."
          - "Key finding: sample-then-correct > sample-then-select, but only for object-type perturbations."
      ablation_crm_conditioning:
        bullets:
          - "4-way: obs_only (19.0%) >> perdof (11.0%) ≈ argmin (12.0%) > scalar (9.0%)."
          - "Per-DOF conformal features add NO value over observation features."
          - "Hypothesis: obs features encode task-relevant geometric info; conformal stats are noisy at K=10."
      magnitude_sensitivity:
        bullets:
          - "obs_only stable across norms (35-36% spatial); perdof collapses at norm ≥ 0.2 (31%→26%)."
          - "norm=1.42 catastrophic failure (0%) demonstrates magnitude control necessity."
      per_task_analysis:
        bullets:
          - "Per-task heatmap: CRM helps medium-difficulty tasks; hard tasks (0% baseline) unaffected."
          - "PENDING: seed=43 per-task breakdown."

  discussion:
    target_pages: 0.5
    bullets:
      - "Why per-DOF fails: learned correction can extract uncertainty signals from obs features directly; explicit conformal stats at K=10 are noisy and redundant."
      - "Object vs spatial: object perturbations (category generalization) create correctable action errors; spatial perturbations require replanning, not correction."
      - "Limitations: (1) sim-only, (2) single VLA backbone, (3) some tasks hurt by CRM, (4) magnitude bound needs tuning."

  conclusion:
    target_pages: 0.3
    bullets:
      - "ACR-VLA: learned observation-conditioned correction after conformal selection improves VLA robustness on object perturbations (+7.0pp)."
      - "Negative result: per-DOF conformal features do not improve correction — cautionary for uncertainty-conditioned policy correction."
      - "Future: multi-backbone validation, real robot transfer, adaptive magnitude scheduling."

## Task: Write Method Section for CoRL 2026 Paper

Write the complete Method section (Section 3) for the ACR-VLA paper targeting CoRL 2026. Output a single LaTeX file.

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing, Read the LaTeX writing skill at `/home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md` for formatting standards.

### Paper Context

**Title**: "Sample, Select, Correct: Observation-Conditioned Residual Refinement for Robust VLA Control"

**Core Claim**: A lightweight observation-conditioned residual module (CRM), applied after multi-sample conformal selection on a frozen VLA, improves object manipulation success by +7.0pp over sample selection alone. Per-DOF conformal features provide NO additional benefit over observation features (honest negative result). Correction magnitude control is critical.

**Pipeline**: Frozen VLA → K=10 samples → CGS scoring → argmin selection → CRM correction (magnitude-bounded) → final action

### Section Structure (target: ~2 pages, CoRL format)

Write `\section{Method}` with these subsections:

#### 3.1 Problem Setup
- Frozen flow-matching VLA π_θ generates K action samples per control step
- Action space: 7-DOF (6 arm + 1 gripper), action chunks of length C=50, but only first H=5 steps used (receding horizon)
- Gripper handled separately outside the pipeline (direct thresholding)
- Goal: improve action quality at inference time without retraining π_θ

#### 3.2 Multi-Sample Generation and Selection
- Draw K=10 samples via independent flow-matching rollouts
- Retain first H=5 steps of each chunk
- Compute Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage covariance per horizon step (cite ledoit2004well):
  Σ_h = (1-α_LW) * Σ_emp + α_LW * (tr(Σ_emp)/d) * I
  where d/K = 0.6, shrinkage reduces eigenvalue estimation error from 30-40% to below 5%
- Mahalanobis nonconformity score: s_h(a) = (a - μ_h)^T Σ_h^{-1} (a - μ_h)
- **Argmin selection**: a_base = argmin_{k} Σ_h s_h(a^(k)) — selects sample with lowest total nonconformity across horizon steps
- This selection step already exploits cross-DOF covariance structure (cite braun2025cgs)
- Note: this argmin selection is our primary baseline — it approximates ReconVLA's (cite chen2026reconvla) conformal selection strategy

#### 3.3 Conformal Residual Module (CRM)
- CRM is a lightweight 2-layer MLP (~N parameters, use placeholder `${\sim}$N` with `% TODO: exact param count pending from checkpoint`)
- **Input**: frozen observation embedding z_obs from base VLA encoder
- **Output**: residual correction δ ∈ R^{d×H} = R^30
- **Magnitude-bounded correction**: a* = a_base + clip(δ, ‖δ‖₂ ≤ ε)
  where ε is a norm bound hyperparameter
- The CRM does NOT receive CGS features or uncertainty statistics as input. It relies solely on observation features. This is a deliberate design choice validated by ablation (Section 5): observation features already encode sufficient task-relevant information for correction, while per-DOF conformal statistics add noise at the K=10 sample budget.
- Training: offline with L2 loss: L = ‖a* - a_expert‖² on demonstration trajectories from LIBERO (cite liu2023libero)
- Training data: 26,737 precomputed samples from 10 demonstrations per task across 20 tasks
- For each demo step: run K=10 SmolVLA forward passes, compute CGS, select argmin sample as a_base
- Augmentation: additive Gaussian noise on mean-action vector (σ ∈ [0.02, 0.1]) and uncertainty features (σ ≈ 0.006)
- Instantiated on SmolVLA (cite shukor2025smolvla), 450M-parameter flow-matching VLA

#### 3.4 Magnitude Control
- **Critical finding**: unbounded correction (norm ≈ 1.42, the natural CRM output range) causes catastrophic 0% success — compounding error destroys the trajectory
- Small ε (0.05-0.2) yields stable correction; we use ε=0.1 as default
- This connects to the residual policy literature: Silver et al. (cite silver2018residual) introduced bounded residual corrections; TRANSIC (cite jiang2024transic) uses learned binary gating; PLD (cite xiao2026pld) schedules magnitude bounds
- ACR-VLA's approach: fixed norm clipping — simple but effective. The key insight is that any learned residual correction on a frozen VLA must be magnitude-constrained to prevent compounding error
- Observation-conditioned CRM (obs_only) is uniquely robust across norm values (35-36% spatial), while per-DOF-conditioned variants collapse at high norms — further evidence that obs features provide more stable conditioning

#### 3.5 Inference Protocol
- Brief description of one control step: draw K samples → CGS score → argmin select → CRM correct (with clip) → execute first action → re-plan
- Total overhead: K=10 extra forward passes through base VLA + ~3ms CRM inference
- No retraining of base model

- Training-time: RobustVLA \cite{robustvla2025}（RL post-training + Jacobian regularization）, SRPO \cite{srpo2025}（self-referential RL fine-tuning）, DiG-Flow \cite{digflow2025}（discrepancy-guided flow matching regularization）, TT-VLA \cite{liu2026ttvla}（test-time RL adaptation with progress rewards）. 共同局限：需要 retraining 或 per-task RL
- Inference-time: ReconVLA \cite{chen2026reconvla}（conformal prediction for multi-sample selection + failure detection; CRITICAL: 正确描述为 conformal prediction method, 不是 "scalar Euclidean distance"。我们的 argmin baseline 是 "a simplified selection baseline inspired by ReconVLA's conformal selection frontend"）, SC-VLA \cite{liu2026scvla}（online action refinement via sparse world imagination + residual RL; needs task-level RL, not plug-and-play）, VLA-Pilot \cite{li2025vlapilot}（evolutionary diffusion optimization with MLLM verifier; 2.41s per step, too slow for real-time）, A2C2 \cite{a2c2_2025}（asynchronous action chunk correction; applies correction unconditionally without first selecting a high-quality starting action）
- **定位 ACR-VLA**：inference-time, plug-and-play, no retraining, combines conformal selection WITH learned correction（selection alone is upper-bounded by sample quality; correction alone lacks a good starting point）

**\subsection{Conformal Prediction in Robotics}**
- CP foundations: Angelopoulos \cite{angelopoulos2023gentle}（gentle intro）, CGS \cite{braun2025cgs}（Mahalanobis-based multivariate conformal scoring — our scoring method）
- CP in robotics: Conformalized teleoperation \cite{zhao2024conformalized}（CP for high-DOF robot action uncertainty detection in teleoperation）, CP-Loop \cite{wang2025cploop}（feedback-based CP for trajectory optimization）, ACP+CBF \cite{zhou2025acp_cbf}（adaptive CP + control barrier functions for safe RL）
- **定位 ACR-VLA**：uses CP for sample selection stage, but does NOT claim formal coverage guarantees for the corrected output. CP serves as a scoring mechanism, not as a calibration tool.

**\subsection{Residual Policy Learning}**
- Silver et al. \cite{silver2018residual}（first residual policy framework: zero-init + bounded corrections on classical controllers）
- TRANSIC \cite{jiang2024transic}（learned binary gating for sim-to-real residual corrections; demonstrates ungated correction → model collapse）
- PLD \cite{xiao2026pld}（scheduled magnitude bound ξ for residual RL on VLAs, validated on LIBERO）
- DRC \cite{pan2025drc}（temporal decay of correction magnitude over episode）
- **Magnitude control 是关键关联**：Silver 用 residual scaling, TRANSIC 用 binary gating, PLD 用 scheduling, DRC 用 temporal decay. ACR-VLA 用 fixed L2 norm clipping — 最简单的方案，但我们 systematically 研究了这个在 VLA inference-time correction 领域被忽视的超参数。
- **关键区别**：上述方法都需要 RL training; ACR-VLA 的 CRM 是 supervised offline training（L2 loss to demonstrations），不需要 reward function 或 environment interaction

**\subsection{Uncertainty Quantification for VLAs}**
- DiU \cite{xing2026diu}（single-pass UQ for flow matching via velocity divergence — closed-form posterior covariance）
- SAFE \cite{gu2025safe}（multitask failure detection using VLA internal features + CP for detection timing）
- VLA calibration \cite{zollo2025vla_calibration}（first systematic study of confidence calibration in VLAs; prompt ensembles + Platt scaling）
- **定位 ACR-VLA**：multi-sample UQ（K=10 forward passes）vs single-pass methods. We use uncertainty for action selection, not for failure detection or calibration. Our negative result on per-DOF conformal features as CRM input connects to the broader challenge of using uncertainty estimates as decision-making features.
